A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Lizard and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Content can be matched across the substantial reorganization, with no material reading gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, synthetic passkey retrieval, efficiency measurements and ablations, including additional small-model results in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds LongBench evaluations in Appendix E, Table 9.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 revises the local-attention component: v1 attends to meta-token keys and values, whereas v3 uses learnable scalar sinks only in the denominator, without meta-token value contributions. This changes the reported procedure beyond renaming it Anchor Window Attention. Gated attention, Hedgehog maps and the two-stage training framework remain.

E1.justification: v3 adds six LongBench datasets in Appendix E and Table 9: 2WikiMultihopQA, HotpotQA, MultiNews, PassageRetrieval-en, LCC and RepoBench-P. This substantially broadens evaluation coverage beyond the retained standard benchmarks and synthetic passkey retrieval. Alpaca training coverage remains unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Liger-GLA-Mistral-7B and Liger-GLA-Llama-3-8B as evaluated comparators. Existing comparators remain, including the same three models in the recall evaluation and the same gating alternatives in Table 3.

E3.justification: The added LongBench evaluation uses Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and its Lizard variant, introducing a new model configuration. Existing training budgets, hyperparameters, synthetic-retrieval procedures and efficiency settings are retained. LongBench scoring metrics, context limits and other evaluation details are not specified.

E4.justification: The gating-design, window/meta-token, component-removal and LoRA-rank ablations retain the same entries and findings in Tables 3–6. The synthetic length-generalization evaluation and sample generations are also unchanged. LongBench supplies additional benchmark results rather than a new ablation or diagnostic analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations or significance tests for its experiments. The additional result rows do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 9 adds results across six LongBench datasets, including teacher/Lizard scores of 18.3/19.6 on HotpotQA, 28.5/27.8 on MultiNews and 48.6/52.7 on RepoBench-P. Table 1 adds Liger MMLU scores of 36.3 for Mistral and 43.4 for Llama. Shared benchmark scores, ablations and recall/efficiency plots remain unchanged; these additions do not establish performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: v3 changes the mathematical definition of local-attention normalization and corrects autoregressive conditioning from x1:i, which includes the target token, to x<i in Section 3.2. The complexity claims and exponential gate-factorization argument remain. No theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The central performance-recovery and length-generalization claims persist. The headline MMLU advantage changes from 18 points, or 8–18 in v1’s contributions, to 9.4–24.5 points against LoLCATs and Liger. The introductory throughput claim changes from 24% to 32%, although v1 already reports 32% elsewhere.

C2.justification: v3 interprets meta-memory as attention sinks that absorb attention mass and manage massive activations, replacing v1’s compressed-global-representation explanation. Section 5.4 also adds the hypothesis that overly wide windows introduce noise or distract from global context. The backbone-dependence and recall-memory limitations are unchanged, moving from Appendix A to Section 6.

D1.justification: Section 4 newly documents GEMM, the mma.sync instruction and cuBLAS/FlashAttention backends, and states that custom CUDA kernels are avoided. v1 describes tensor-core-compatible chunkwise computation more generally. This expands implementation documentation without establishing a backend change; Table 7 and existing resource/access information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds substantive discussion of Liger’s parameter-free pooling gates and new activation/sink references by Sun et al. and Gu et al. It replaces the vision-RoPE citation with Su et al.’s RoFormer and removes several hybrid/streaming references. The broader linearization positioning remains; GLA and LoLCATs publication updates refer to retained works.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, preliminaries and method exposition are extensively rewritten. Hardware implementation becomes a separate Section 4, limitations move into the main text, and the standalone conclusion disappears. Terminology changes to Anchor Window Attention, with substantial restructuring beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: The document changes from one-column to two-column formatting, with extensive resizing and relocation of displays. v3 replaces the separate training-pipeline and attention-map figures with a combined architecture Figure 1, enlarges the efficiency display, expands Table 1 and adds Table 9. Retained appendix tables are substantially repositioned.

improvement.justification: The Liger comparison and six LongBench evaluations modestly strengthen empirical coverage, while the revised architecture figure and separate hardware discussion improve clarity. These gains are limited by sparse LongBench evaluation details and the unexplained relationship between the revised sink formulation and retained results. v3 also introduces a numerical inconsistency: its claimed 21.9-point Liger-to-teacher MMLU gap disagrees with Table 1, which implies 23.2 or 26.1 points.
